newsitem.title: USA: She came to the inauguration and stayed on.
newsitem.headline: She came to the inauguration and stayed on.

text.p: Lucille Williams is a surprise front-row guest at President Clinton's inaugural parade Monday.

Williams, 85 and a big Clinton supporter, thought she was a special guest at Clinton's inauguration when a big package of inaugural trinkets and a letter saying she was invited "to attend and participate in the inauguration of William Jefferson Clinton" arrived at her Los Angeles home.

The committee organising Clinton's $30 million second inauguration did not really mean she would actually have a ticket to get into any of the main events, just that she could take her chances like anyone else. They sent out 500,000 similar "invitations" to Clinton campaign volunteers as tokens of thanks.

She flew into Dulles Airport, booked into the Holiday Inn and was shocked to learn she was not among the annointed big contributors and Friends of Bill with entry to all the coveted galas, balls, parade and actual ceremony.
Not to worry. The local press picked up her plight and as soon as you could say "four more years" the legions of embarrassed inauguration organisers sprang to attention.

Fetched in her wheelchair, she was rolled through a private White House tour, escorted to the gala entertainment bash at the USAir Arena Sunday night, provided a spot at the Clinton swearing-in at the Capitol, parade tickets afterwards and two tickets to the top-tier Arkansas ball Monday night.
"I've had so much attention, I don't know whether to cry or shout," she told the Washington Post.
